symptoms: Dead hearts in vegetative stage; white earheads at reproductive stage
management: Remove stubbles and volunteer rice; synchronize planting and monitor moth activity; seek local threshold-based advice.
guide_reference: TNAU Rice IPM / ICAR Kharif Agro-Advisories

symptoms: Leaves folded lengthwise with scraped white patches
management: Avoid excessive nitrogen; conserve natural enemies; scout regularly and consult KVK if damage increases.

symptoms: Hoppers near plant base; yellowing and hopper-burn patches
management: Avoid excessive nitrogen and indiscriminate sprays; maintain field monitoring and consult local threshold guidance.

symptoms: White streaks on leaves; adult beetles scrape leaf surface
management: Remove badly affected leaves where practical; keep field edges clean and monitor crop.

symptoms: Silver shoot or onion-like tiller with no panicle
management: Use locally recommended tolerant varieties and remove affected tillers; ask KVK for local incidence guidance.

symptoms: Diamond-shaped lesions with grey centre and brown margin
management: Use resistant varieties where recommended; avoid excess nitrogen and maintain balanced nutrition.

symptoms: Yellowing from leaf tip or margin with wavy lesions
management: Use clean seed and resistant varieties; avoid moving contaminated water and maintain field sanitation.

symptoms: Oval green-grey lesions on leaf sheath near waterline
management: Avoid dense canopy and excess nitrogen; remove crop residues and monitor spread.

symptoms: Tiny white insects fly from leaf underside; sticky honeydew
management: Remove alternate weed hosts, use yellow sticky traps for monitoring and avoid excess nitrogen.

symptoms: Clusters of soft-bodied insects on tender shoots; leaf curling
management: Monitor colonies, conserve predators and avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum sprays.

symptoms: Leaf edges yellow then redden; downward curling
management: Use locally recommended tolerant varieties and monitor leaf symptoms regularly.

symptoms: Silvery streaks and distorted young leaves
management: Scout early, manage weeds and avoid unnecessary insecticide use that harms beneficial insects.

symptoms: Rosette flowers; larvae damage developing bolls
management: Destroy crop residues after harvest, avoid ratooning and follow timely crop termination advice.

symptoms: Bore holes in squares, flowers or bolls; frass near holes
management: Scout squares and bolls, use pheromone traps for monitoring and follow threshold-based IPM advice.

symptoms: Leaf curling, vein thickening and enations on underside
management: Remove severely affected plants early where advised; manage whitefly and remove alternate weed hosts.

symptoms: White waxy colonies on stems and leaf joints; sticky growth
management: Remove infested weeds and crop residues; monitor field borders and seek confirmation before intervention.

symptoms: Red insects on bolls; stained lint and damaged seeds
management: Remove alternate hosts and leftover cotton; harvest timely and maintain field sanitation.

symptoms: Round holes in fruits with frass; caterpillar may be inside
management: Collect and destroy damaged fruits and caterpillars; use marigold trap crop and pheromone monitoring as in IPM guidance.

symptoms: Small white insects under leaves; leaf yellowing or curling
management: Use yellow sticky traps, remove alternate weed hosts and monitor for virus symptoms.

symptoms: Winding pale tunnels inside leaf tissue
management: Remove badly mined leaves where practical; seek local confirmation before any treatment.
guide_reference: TNAU Tomato Crop Protection Guide – Serpentine leaf miner

symptoms: Colonies on tender shoots; sticky honeydew and curling
management: Remove heavily infested weeds, conserve natural enemies and check nearby plants.

symptoms: Silvery scars on leaves and flower damage
management: Use field sanitation and monitoring; check for virus symptoms and seek local identification.

symptoms: Brown concentric target-like spots on older leaves
management: Remove infected lower leaves, avoid wetting foliage late in day and rotate crops.

symptoms: Water-soaked lesions that rapidly turn brown; white growth in humid conditions
management: Improve air movement, avoid prolonged leaf wetness and seek urgent local diagnosis during outbreaks.

symptoms: Seedlings collapse at soil line; patchy nursery gaps
management: Use raised, well-drained nursery beds, avoid overcrowding and prevent water stagnation.
